title: Lineage2Elbera reuse audit
summary: Audit of the upstream Lineage2Elbera reference checkout across 22 listed entries, recommending which components to adapt, reference or defer, plus verification limits and a reuse rule for later work.
scope: BSP reuse and vendored reader symbols
NPC animation selectors and notify fixtures
armor slot tables and mesh export
upstream license (MIT with exclusions, ISC nested package)
notes: Classified DOC by manifest (MANIFEST_TYPE authoritative). Source has no frontmatter and no ADR status field; it contains a '## Decision' section but no Context/Consequences structure, so it is an audit report, not an ADR. Owner/dated decisions and work-order statements recorded for synthesizer conflict detection: (1) '## Decision' (dated 2026-11-07): 'Use Lineage2Elbera as a source of reusable implementations, fixtures and format knowledge before writing another decoder.' (2) '## Conclusions for every listed entry': per-entry verdicts Adapt/Reference/Defer, e.g. 'world' 'Strong candidate: reuse BSP render-section/lightmap parsing'; 'src' 'Character assembly changes weights, attachment and timing, conflicting with current preservation guarantees'; 'upscale' 'Defer AI upscaling for source-fidelity work'; 'dev' 'Defer upstream server and database seeding scripts'. (3) '## Recommended proofs before implementation' item 1: 'Baked BSP lighting is the strongest visible-content candidate', requiring verification of a lit node in UE123/licensee28 '20_20.Model798' first, and a separate Babylon comparison before claiming visible benefit. Item 3: animation/audio changes require comparison before change. (4) '## Reuse rule for subsequent work': 'Prefer pinned upstream functions plus a small adapter when they preserve the required data.' The document states it does not implement upstream fixes and does not claim the lighting proof passed. Native verifier Engine SHA-256 differs from this client's recorded Engine.dll; do not remove gates.
